text:
raj: quick heads-up — ran the longtail recall sweep with new centroid pooling (v2-centroid) and saw a weird recall@2 drop vs avg-pool. gist: https://gist.github.com/placeholder
maya: link? numbers?
raj: paste block:
```
model v2-centroid | recall@1 0.70 | recall@2 0.62 | recall@5 0.82
model v1-avg      | recall@1 0.71 | recall@2 0.68 | recall@5 0.83
dataset: longtail-10k
```
leah: that's odd — recall@1 similar but recall@2 down = ordering/near-neighbor shift, maybe cluster fragmentation
tony: did you quantize? int8 can change distances nonlinearly :thinking:
raj: yes int8 per-channel, onnxruntime, config: pool=centroid, normalize=false (oops?)
maya: ah normalize=false could explain it — centroids require l2 norm usually. can you rerun with normalize=true?
eval-bot: automated-eval: run 1777777001-1 completed. metrics: recall@1 0.705, recall@2 0.672, recall@5 0.829, kendall_tau 0.012
raj: rerun shows normalize=true fixes most of it. still small ordering flips on tail queries. attaching small sample
raj: sample (query / top3 ids):
```
q: "how to update invoice"
centroid-top3: [123, 456, 789]
avg-top3:      [123, 789, 456]
```
leah: that's classic centroid leakage — tokens that appear across docs pull centroid toward common tokens; avg handles differently. maybe use TF-IDF weighting when computing centroid
tony: or hybrid pool: avg + centroid concat then PCA/linproj; also try cosine after norm.
maya: can we run a quick ablation: centroid+tfidf, centroid+norm, avg, concat on 1k sample tonight? if yes I'll schedule
raj: scheduling now. leaving notes: run on deduped-longtail, seed 42, k=5, k=2 recall targets, add per-query top swaps list
eval-bot: queued job 1777777001-2. ETA ~45m
maya: great. if centroid+tfidf recovers recall@2 we can keep centroid for speed. if not, fallback to avg or concat.
leah: also add silhouette/cluster-size histogram — centroid fragmentation if cluster sizes tiny
raj: will add. thanks all :thumbsup:
